contribution.text: Seed proposal 01 (PR #163). Layered settings and a permission engine so every behaviour is configuration and the default is read-only. Review questions: Are the layers, locks and fail-safe reload the right shape, and is the precedence unambiguous? | Does deny-beats-ask-beats-allow, with an unmatched write refused in `read-only`, match the intent "model it after your own default settings"? | Is the floor (merge, push, review, attest) correctly placed in code and kept out of settings? | Is the `auto` gate (user layer only) strong enough? | The code for the first step is in lane C120 (`foundation/crates/hud_core`, contract `contracts/hud-settings-v1.md`); review that separately.

Seed proposal 02 (PR #164). A transport-free HUD core with an MCP adapter and a read-first agent API so models ping the hall for cards, work and availability. Review questions: Is one core with several adapters (MCP, loopback HTTP, in-process) the right split? | Is the read-first agent API (card, work, availability, events, result) the right set, with `ETag`/304 and sequence-numbered events? | Are the security properties (separate human and agent doors, hashed per-seat tokens, body caps, data-not-instructions) sufficient? | Does folding the registrar's five MCP tools into core operations beat running two servers?

Seed proposal 03 (PR #165). Run the hall on the local network with a roster of seats, guild workers and instances, and one hall per repository and machine. Review questions: Is the operator-versus-instance split right, and is the roster in the table correct? | Is pull-and-heartbeat with hall-clock leases a sound way to handle two machines? | Are the wire requirements (named bind address, encrypted path, accepted Host list, per-instance hashed tokens) enough for a LAN? | Does the domain and crossplay arrangement keep the dependency direction (devtools on Aaroneous, never the reverse) and the product's gate intact?

Seed proposal 04 (PR #166). Cut token cost with tiered routing, content-addressed packs, conditional responses, caches and measured dense handles. Review questions: Is the ranking of the techniques sensible, and is accounting (item 8) the precondition for claiming any saving? | Is the dense-handle policy (measured per backend, opaque handles only, plain text where the model must read) the right use of the base-encoding idea? | Re-run Appendix A on another tokenizer if you have one; the finding depends on how a tokenizer splits digits.

Seed proposal 05 (PR #167). Per-model prompt profiles and adapters, chosen by measurement and reviewed as files. Review questions: Is moving per-model knowledge (such as the calibrated system prompt for Qwen) into data and a pure adapter the right design? | Do the guardrails (wording, format and parameters only; round-trip check that every confirmed slot reaches the prompt) hold? | Is tuning on one split and confirming on a held-out split enough to avoid overfitting the test?

Seed proposal 06 (PR #168). Turn an inquiry into a typed job and a survey into a pre-built brief that compiles deterministically into one background prompt. Review questions: Is "the light model never writes the final prompt; it fills slots, software compiles" the right division? | Are the slot states (`empty`, `derived`, `proposed`, `confirmed`, `unverified`) and the completeness gate enough to keep a wrong guess from slipping through? | Does this extend the C106 intake record and the existing packet types, rather than creating a third format?

Seed proposal 07 (PR #169). Local models as advisory guild workers on a low-permission queue, staff roles as job cards, and inspection access. Review questions: Are the four worker classes (W0 to W3) the right set, and is each cheaply checkable by software? | Is "no repository writes, no branches, no PRs" for workers the intended boundary for now? | Is the inspector role (specific actions, never the floor) the right meaning of "admin"? | The conflict with `LOCAL_MODEL_AUTONOMY_POLICY.md` (which lets the local model draft bounded changes and use `promote`): reconcile it, or keep the HUD's narrower default and record the difference.

Seed proposal 08 (PR #170). Roles, a taste-versus-correctness boundary, skill-gated delegation and trust earned from reviewed outcomes. Review questions: Is the taste/correctness boundary right, including "the system names the gate and offers the nearest option that passes"? | Is a per-skill trust level, with promotion and demotion from independent reviewed outcomes, the right mechanism? Is `can_take` as a pure function with golden vectors the right form? | Is "outside benchmarks are priors, promotion rests on our own deterministic milestone suites" the right policy? | Are the identity and consent rules for users and contributors adequate for a first version on the owner's own machines?

Seed proposal 09 (PR #171). A 3D analogy-reference view, a light exploration layer, and a staged digital twin built from the owner's stated preferences. Review questions: Is the reading of "analogy reference" (concepts, documents, lanes and components linked by analogies with mappings, strength and evidence) right? CONFIRMED by the owner. | Is 3D one view next to 2D panels, with the same graph readable as a list, the right scope? | Do the exploration guardrails (rewards for confirmed evidence, no streaks or loss mechanics) and the psychology scope (elicitation of stated wants, no trait or mood inference) hold? | Is the staged twin (preference log, proposed slots only, measured acceptance, then maybe more) the right order, and is it correctly kept inside Aaroneous's `.si` twin concept?

Seed proposal 10 (PR #172). A standard native Rust application embedding the core, an operations panel over Guild, and reuse of other Rust tools behind workspace traits. Review questions: Is the native-app-embeds-the-core design right, with the webview kept only as a fallback? | Is the spike's pass condition (the packet editor first) the right test of a toolkit? | Are the seams (model backend, context store, event source, operation, classifier) the right traits to carve first? | Is the import policy (clean-room patterns over heavy runtimes; admission scoring for anything entering the product) respected?

Seed proposal 11 (PR #173). Let the most capable qualified machine host the hall, first by owner-pinned single-host leadership and manual fenced handoff, and only later by unattended failover once a durable fencing authority exists. Review questions: Is "qualification selects, the fencing authority decides" the right split, and is the compare-and-swap on `(term, host)` a sound linearization point? | Does write-ahead fencing of the incumbent close the recovery hole, and is every partial state covered? | Are the invariants (at most one valid writer across all terms; no duplicate observable operation; SafeHold on uncertainty) the right ones? | Is stage A a reasonable first version, with B and C gated on evidence?

Seed proposal 12 (PR #174). Build devtools modularly and Aaroneous-compliant by construction, with a thin stable base and a thick frontier, so proven components can graduate into Aaroneous. Review questions: Are the rings and the flow (frontier, base, Aaroneous) the right structure for "thin base, thick frontier"? | Is the checklist a faithful reading of the product rules, and is it right to leave hot-path and memory-geometry rules to `kernel` crates? | Is the measured table honest about what the auditor does and does not prove? | Is running the product's tools on devtools in CI acceptable with respect to the dependency direction?

Seed proposal 13 (PR #176). One job-card schema (card, record, evidence tiers), a retrieval order for context packs, and a validated plan graph for work that decomposes. Review questions: Is "thin card, thick evidence, attached by tier" the right balance, and are the required fields the right minimum? | Is it right to extend the existing formats (steward card, intake, topic-case receipt) rather than define a new one? | Is the retrieval order (structural, lexical, then vector only if measured) right for this corpus, and is the citation rule enforceable? | Are the plan-validity rules enough to stop a model-proposed graph from bypassing the gates?

Seed proposal 14 (PR #177). An operating review of the tasking, scheduling and delegation system: measured bottlenecks, missing components, time and tick design, departments, internal affairs, and how much model-driven work software can take over. Review questions: Do the findings follow from the evidence cited, and are there bottlenecks I missed? | Is incremental, bounded-parallel scanning the right first fix, and is the rate-limit risk handled? | Are tick classes and departments useful structure or needless ceremony at the current scale? | Is the internal-affairs design independent enough, and are consequences kept inside the trust ledger?
